content.text:
I've reviewed the full agreement for any supply-side exclusivity. Here's what I found:

- **Article II (p0030, p0043)** — the grant is expressly a **non-exclusive** license, running both ways; Licensor may license to others, and nothing restricts Licensee's sourcing.
- **Article IV/V (p0049, p0050, p0052, p0078)** — repeatedly styled "Non Exclusive license"; fees are volume-banded with no minimum commitment or "all requirements" undertaking.
- **Restrictions (p0027, p0035–p0047, p0085)** — standard IP/scope restrictions on use, sublicensing and reverse engineering of the *Licensed Technology*; they do not bar us from procuring competing FX platform services.
- **Article XXII ROFR (p0139–p0141)** — a right of first refusal on a *sale of assets / merger* of Licensee, not on future work or procurement; a change-of-control matter outside this rule.
- **Article XX (p0134)** and **Article X(b) (p0125)** — change-of-control consent and a non-solicit of employees; neither is an exclusive-dealing covenant.

No exclusivity, sole-supplier or requirements obligation binds us, so the preferred position is met.

input.quote: Licensee acknowledges that the grant of the license set forth in this Section is a non-exclusive license and that the Licensor shall have the right to use and to license to other parties the Licensed Technology for any purpose and in any manner as Licensor may determine in its sole discretion.
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no exclusivity, sole-supplier or requirements obligation on us, which meets the preferred position (no exclusivity binding Customer). The grant is expressly non-exclusive in both directions (p0030, p0043, p0049, p0050), the volume-banded user fees carry no minimum-volume or "all requirements" commitment, and nothing bars us from licensing or using competing FX platform services. The Article II restrictions (p0027, p0035-p0047, p0085) are ordinary scope/IP protections over the Licensed Technology itself rather than exclusive-dealing covenants. The Article XXII Right of First Refusal (p0139-p0141) applies only to a bona fide third-party offer to buy our assets or merge with us - a change-of-control right, not a first refusal on future work or procurement - so it does not restrict our freedom to buy from other suppliers and is outside this rule (the change-of-control consent in p0134 and the employee non-solicit in p0125 are likewise not exclusivity). No redline required under this rule; the corporate ROFR and change-of-control consent may warrant separate review under the assignment/change-of-control rule.
